sentences.en: Back in the 1960s and 70s in the city of Pittsburgh, there was a nickname for guys like John Moon,
sentences.zh: 回到20世纪60和70年代的匹兹堡市，当时人们给约翰·穆恩这类人起了一个绰号，

sentences.en: Which simply meant that no matter where you went for a job, nobody would hire you.
sentences.zh: 意思很简单，无论你去哪里找工作，都没人会雇佣你。

sentences.en: Moon grew up in Pittsburgh's largely black and economically depressed Hill District.
sentences.zh: 穆恩在匹兹堡的希尔区长大，那里主要是黑人聚居区，经济萧条。

sentences.en: In better times, the Hill had its own Negro League baseball team and jazz clubs that hosted
sentences.zh: 在更好的时期，希尔区曾拥有自己的黑人联盟棒球队，还有接待过
艾灵顿公爵和路易斯·阿姆斯特朗的爵士俱乐部。

sentences.en: But by the time Moon was graduating high school in the late 1960s, there was no escaping the
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪60年代末穆恩高中毕业时，他已经无法逃脱
社区被贴上的“不可雇佣”的标签。

sentences.en: I don't want to go to the Hill because you may get beat up.
sentences.zh: 我不想去希尔区，因为你可能会被打。

sentences.en: You have drug addicts and alcoholics.
sentences.zh: 那里有吸毒者和酗酒者。

sentences.en: And that same label was placed on myself and I understood that.
sentences.zh: 同样的标签也贴在了我身上，我明白这一点。

sentences.en: But just because that was your thought doesn't necessarily mean that I had to live up to it.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅因为那是你们的想法，并不一定意味着我必须活成那样。

sentences.en: So Moon was glad to land a well-paying job right out of school at the local steel mill, only
sentences.zh: 所以穆恩很高兴一毕业就在当地的钢铁厂找到了一份高薪工作，但很快

sentences.en: to discover that the hours weren't as reliable as he had hoped.
sentences.zh: 发现工作时间并不像他希望的那样稳定。

sentences.en: Next, he was an orderly at Pittsburgh's Presbyterian University Hospital, which provided steady
sentences.zh: 接下来，他在匹兹堡长老会大学医院当护工，虽然提供了稳定的
工作，但除此之外别无其他。

sentences.en: All I was doing was making beds and taking people back and forth to the operating room
sentences.zh: 我所做的只是铺床、把病人送进送出手术室，

sentences.en: and lifting and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 还有搬运东西之类的活儿。

sentences.en: Mechanical things where you didn't have to think.
sentences.zh: 不需要动脑筋的机械性工作。

sentences.en: For a while, Moon tried his best to find meaning in the work.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，穆恩尽力在工作中寻找意义。

sentences.en: But there was a part of me that said, there has to be something more that I can do.
sentences.zh: 但我内心深处有个声音说，我能做的肯定不止这些。

sentences.en: Then one night, halfway through the graveyard shift, Moon watched as two men burst through
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，在深夜班进行到一半时，穆恩看到两个人冲进了

sentences.en: They were working desperately to save a dying patient.
sentences.zh: 他们正在拼命抢救一名垂死的病人。

sentences.en: And as they rushed by, Moon stood pressed against the wall and wondered.
sentences.zh: 当他们匆匆跑过时，穆恩紧贴着墙站着，心生好奇。

sentences.en: You know, how did they get to be able to do that?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们是怎么学会做这些的？

sentences.en: Maybe today, he wouldn't bat an eye at this scene.
sentences.zh: 也许在今天，他会对这一幕视而不见。

sentences.en: But in 1970, nothing about it made sense.
sentences.zh: 但在1970年，这一切都让人费解。

sentences.en: The two men weren't doctors and they weren't nurses.
sentences.zh: 这两个人既不是医生，也不是护士。

sentences.en: And their strange white uniforms weren't hospital issue.
sentences.zh: 他们奇怪的白色制服也不是医院配发的。

sentences.en: But these guys came in with a certain type of confidence that was just shocking to me from
sentences.zh: 但这些人走进房间时带着一种自信，这让我感到非常震惊，

sentences.en: the very point that they came into the room.
sentences.zh: 从他们进门的那一刻起就是如此。

sentences.en: And they had an emblem on their breasts that just piqued my intereSt.
sentences.zh: 他们的胸前有一个徽章，引起了我的兴趣。

sentences.en: The emblem was the two-snaked caduceus, the traditional sign of medicine and healing.
sentences.zh: 那个徽章是双蛇杖，是医学和治愈的传统标志。

sentences.en: But just below the familiar symbol was a word John Moon had never seen before.
sentences.zh: 但在熟悉的符号下方，有一个约翰·穆恩从未见过的词。

sentences.en: Moon wasn't familiar with the term paramedic.
sentences.zh: 穆恩对“急救员”这个词并不熟悉。

sentences.en: Because back then, no one was.
sentences.zh: 因为在当时，没人熟悉这个词。

sentences.en: Moon was witnessing the birth of a new profession.
sentences.zh: 穆恩正在见证一个新职业的诞生。

sentences.en: One that would go on to change the face of emergency medicine.
sentences.zh: 一个将改变急诊医学面貌的职业。

sentences.en: But to Moon, perhaps the most striking thing of all
sentences.zh: 但对穆恩来说，也许最引人注目的是

sentences.en: was that these first-ever paramedics looked like him.
sentences.zh: 这些史上首批急救员长得和他一样。

sentences.en: I'm standing here looking at these two guys and I'm saying to myself,
sentences.zh: 我站在那里看着这两个人，心想，

sentences.en: my God, these are black guys.
Never before had Moon seen young African-American men performing that kind of work.
sentences.zh: 穆恩从未见过年轻的非裔美国人从事那种工作。

sentences.en: These were two guys that had afros and beards.
sentences.zh: 这两个人留着爆炸头，蓄着胡子。

sentences.en: And the staff on the floor gave them a level of respect that amazed me.
sentences.zh: 楼层的医护人员对他们表现出的尊重让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And there's something I never really mentioned to anyone is I actually snuck off of the floor.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事我从未对任何人提起过，那就是我其实偷偷溜出了楼层。

sentences.en: And I actually followed them out to the vehicle because I wanted to see what prompted them to show such proudness and boldness.
sentences.zh: 我跟着他们到了车边，因为我想看看是什么让他们表现得如此自豪和大胆。

sentences.en: Once I looked at that vehicle, pull off, it was almost like, there goes my job.
sentences.zh: 当我看着那辆车开走时，我心想，我的工作有着落了。
我的职业生涯有着落了。

sentences.en: That's what I want to do.
Moon vowed right then, halfway through his long night shift, to become a paramedic.
sentences.zh: 穆恩就在那个漫长夜班的中途发誓，要成为一名急救员。

sentences.en: And in Pittsburgh, in 1970, the only place to do that was an organization called Freedom House Ambulance Service.
sentences.zh: 在1970年的匹兹堡，唯一能实现这一目标的地方是一个叫“自由之家救护车服务”的组织。

sentences.en: So I went and applied to get a job with them.
sentences.zh: 所以我去申请了那里的工作。

sentences.en: But that history about how a group of young black men from Pittsburgh became the world's first paramedics
sentences.zh: 但关于一群来自匹兹堡的年轻黑人如何成为世界上第一批急救员的历史，
我自己也是一名前急救员。

sentences.en: I did this job for 10 years.
And you'd think the profession's origin story would be a big deal.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为这个职业的起源故事应该很重要。

sentences.en: But the truth is, most of the EMTs I've talked to have never heard of the Freedom House paramedics
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我交谈过的大多数急救员（EMT）从未听说过“自由之家”急救员，

sentences.en: or understand what we owe them.
sentences.zh: 也不了解我们欠他们多少。

sentences.en: Today, it's easy to take what paramedics do for granted.
sentences.zh: 今天，人们很容易把急救员的工作视为理所当然。

sentences.en: Call 911 and they'll arrive with cardiac monitors, airway equipment,
sentences.zh: 拨打911，他们会带着心脏监护仪、气道设备赶到，

sentences.en: and an array of pharmaceuticals to treat anything from heart attacks to gunshots to premature births.
sentences.zh: 还有一系列药物，可以治疗从心脏病发作到枪伤再到早产的任何情况。

sentences.en: But for a long time, emergency medical service, or what today is called EMS,
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，紧急医疗服务，也就是今天所说的EMS，
并不提供任何类似的服务。

sentences.en: In the early days of what we would view as EMS,
sentences.zh: 在我们今天所理解的EMS早期，

sentences.en: it really wasn't the equivalent of what we see today.
sentences.zh: 它真的不是我们今天所看到的那样。

sentences.en: They would do whatever it was they knew to do.
sentences.zh: 他们只会做他们知道该做的事。

sentences.en: But, you know, were they doing the right thing?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他们做对了吗？

sentences.en: He's the president of the EMS Museum and a trained paramedic.
sentences.zh: 他是EMS博物馆馆长，也是一名受过培训的急救员。

sentences.en: Clinchy says that when he started an emergency care in the late 50s,
sentences.zh: 克林奇说，当他在50年代末开始从事急救工作时，

sentences.en: emergency services didn't provide treatment at the scene,
sentences.zh: 急救服务并不在现场提供治疗，

sentences.en: or even necessarily on the way to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 甚至在去医院的路上也不一定提供。

sentences.en: They were just about getting you to the hospital as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们只是尽可能快地把你送到医院。

sentences.en: Which kind of makes sense in a way.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上说得通。

sentences.en: It is, after all, where the doctors are.
But as a result, it often wasn't clear whose responsibility it was to rush to the scene of an accident.
sentences.zh: 但结果是，往往不清楚谁有责任赶到事故现场。

sentences.en: Before the evolution of EMS, who did you call?
Well, I was a paid firefighter back in the 60s, and sometimes we got the call.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在60年代是一名带薪消防员，有时我们会接到电话。

sentences.en: If somebody needed a fire truck and they see it in New York,
sentences.zh: 如果有人需要消防车，在纽约，

sentences.en: You'd pull the handle, and fire personnel and fire equipment would show up.
sentences.zh: 你拉动把手，消防人员和消防设备就会出现。

sentences.en: In other areas, the responsibility for transporting patients often fell to local funeral homes.
sentences.zh: 在其他地区，运送病人的责任通常落在当地的殡仪馆身上。

sentences.en: You're having a massive heart attack, your life's in the balance,
sentences.zh: 你心脏病发作，生命垂危，

sentences.en: and who rolls up to save you?

sentences.zh: 两个开着灵车的殡葬业者。

sentences.en: But in many major cities, this crucial task fell to another municipal service
sentences.zh: 但在许多大城市，这项关键任务落在了另一个市政部门身上，

sentences.en: that probably had even less business responding to medical emergencies, the police.
sentences.zh: 那个部门可能更不应该处理医疗紧急情况，那就是警察。

sentences.en: In the area where I was a firefighter, we had a police department that had a 57 Chevrolet wagon.
sentences.zh: 在我当消防员的地区，我们有一个警察局，他们有一辆57年的雪佛兰旅行车。

sentences.en: That was an emergency response vehicle.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆紧急响应车辆。

sentences.en: So the idea the general public was faced with was more or less what I would call swoop and scoop,
sentences.zh: 所以公众面临的情况多多少少就是我所说的“猛扑和装载”，

sentences.en: which simply meant that you'd call the police, they'd rush the person out there to you,
sentences.zh: 意思很简单，就是你打给警察，他们冲到你那里，

sentences.en: and then they'd pick you up, put you in the back, and rush you back down to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 然后把你抬起来，塞进后座，火速送回医院。

sentences.en: With minimal training and equipment, John Moon says police departments could do little more
sentences.zh: 约翰·穆恩说，由于缺乏培训和设备，警察局几乎做不了什么，

sentences.en: than offer patients basic first aid, a canvas stretcher, a half-empty oxygen tank, and a pillow.
sentences.zh: 只能提供基本的急救、帆布担架、半空的氧气瓶和一个枕头。

sentences.en: Which more often than not, only served to choke off the patient's airway.
sentences.zh: 而这往往只会导致病人的气道阻塞。

sentences.en: And on top of that, both individuals, meaning police officers, got up front and left you back there by yourself.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，两名警察都坐在前排，把你一个人留在后面。

sentences.en: So if you stopped breathing by the time you arrived, you were perhaps DOA because no one had done anything for you.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在到达时停止了呼吸，你可能就死在到院前了，因为没人为你做任何事。

sentences.en: The police simply didn't have the tools, the training, or the disposition to save people in a medical emergency.
sentences.zh: 警察根本没有工具、培训或意愿在医疗紧急情况下救人。

sentences.en: But in the absence of a dedicated emergency medical service, the job was being left to them by default.
sentences.zh: 但在缺乏专门的紧急医疗服务的情况下，这项工作默认留给了他们。

sentences.en: And perhaps nowhere was the problem of relying on the police for help more vividly illustrated than in Pittsburgh's largely black Hill district.
sentences.zh: 也许在匹兹堡主要是黑人聚居的希尔区，依赖警察提供帮助的问题表现得最为生动。

sentences.en: Moon says the city's mostly white police force was often slow to respond to emergencies in the Hill,
sentences.zh: 穆恩说，该市主要是白人的警察部队往往对希尔区的紧急情况反应迟缓，

sentences.en: while the black residents, for their part, were reluctant to even call the police to begin with.
sentences.zh: 而黑人居民则根本不愿意打给警察。

sentences.en: Because there was a trust issue with the police, primarily because there were no constraints.
sentences.zh: 因为存在信任问题，主要是因为警察没有任何约束。

sentences.en: I mean, they could do whatever they wanted, and there was no repercussion or consequences for their actions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们可以为所欲为，而且他们的行为没有任何后果。

sentences.en: No one wanted to get into the exact same police van that the cops had threatened to throw them in the day before.
sentences.zh: 没人想坐进警察前一天威胁要扔他们进去的那种警车里。

sentences.en: So there was issues all the way around.
Do I really want to call the police?
Because chances are they're going to take their time getting here, number one.
sentences.zh: 因为首先，他们很可能会磨磨蹭蹭才到。

sentences.en: And if I wait too long, then chances are a cab won't come to my neighborhood, primarily because of fear of being robbed, or whatever the case is.
sentences.zh: 如果我等太久，出租车也不会来我的社区，主要是因为怕被抢劫，或者其他什么原因。

sentences.en: So the options were very limited during that time.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的选择非常有限。

sentences.en: And the same was true to varying degrees in the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 在全国其他地区，情况在不同程度上也是如此。

sentences.en: Whether a neighborhood was served by the police, or the fire department, or the local funeral home,
sentences.zh: 无论一个社区是由警察、消防局还是当地殡仪馆提供服务，

sentences.en: so long as the priority was transportation as opposed to treatment,
sentences.zh: 只要优先事项是运送而不是治疗，

sentences.en: no one even realized that there was a job that needed doing.
sentences.zh: 甚至没人意识到还有一项工作需要完成。

sentences.en: But then, in the mid-60s, something happened which flipped the paradigm for emergency care on its head,
sentences.zh: 但后来，在60年代中期，发生了一件事，彻底颠覆了急救护理的模式，

sentences.en: and laid the groundwork for the invention of paramedicine.
sentences.zh: 并为急救医学的发明奠定了基础。

sentences.en: In 1966, the federal government published a white paper that would prove so influential
sentences.zh: 1966年，联邦政府发布了一份白皮书，其影响力之大，

sentences.en: that even now, in EMS circles, it is simply called the white paper.
sentences.zh: 以至于即使在今天，在EMS圈子里，它也被简称为“白皮书”。

sentences.en: Basically, it told us we were killing over 50,000 people a year on the highways,
sentences.zh: 基本上，它告诉我们，我们每年在公路上造成超过5万人死亡，

sentences.en: and doing so unnecessarily, that there was a way to intervene and save those people.
sentences.zh: 而且是不必要的，是有办法干预并拯救那些人的。

sentences.en: But we didn't have the people, nor the resources, nor the training to do a whole lot about it.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有人员、资源或培训来做太多事情。

sentences.en: Techniques practiced by combat medics overseas had been largely ignored by the medical community,
sentences.zh: 海外战斗医护人员实践的技术在很大程度上被医学界忽视了，

sentences.en: with the result that a person was more likely to die of a gunshot wound in America
sentences.zh: 结果就是，一个人在美国死于枪伤的可能性，

sentences.en: than on a battlefield in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 比在越南战场上还要大。

sentences.en: The white paper shamed the government into providing money for EMS development on the local level,
sentences.zh: 这份白皮书让政府感到羞愧，从而为地方层面的EMS发展提供了资金，

sentences.en: and government officials and local community leaders began searching for solutions,
sentences.zh: 政府官员和当地社区领袖开始寻找解决方案，

sentences.en: including a community organizer in Pittsburgh named Phil Hallen.
sentences.zh: 其中包括匹兹堡的一位社区组织者，名叫菲尔·哈伦。

sentences.en: Oh my God, why do I do this?
sentences.zh: 天哪，我为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Hallen is a former ambulance attendant who came to Pittsburgh in the early 60s.
sentences.zh: 哈伦是一名前救护车服务员，60年代初来到匹兹堡。

sentences.en: And yes, he hates being interviewed.
Okay, how long are we going to be going on this?
I don't last very long at age 90.
Hallen ran a civil rights organization called the Maurice Falk Medical Fund,
sentences.zh: 哈伦经营着一个名为“莫里斯·福克医学基金”的民权组织，

sentences.en: which examined health disparities due to institutional racism,
sentences.zh: 该组织研究因制度性种族主义导致的健康差异，

sentences.en: and he immediately focused his ire on the city's pitiful emergency services.
sentences.zh: 他立即将愤怒集中在该市可悲的紧急服务上。

sentences.en: What was your impression of the level of care that was available in Pittsburgh?
sentences.zh: 你对匹兹堡当时可用的护理水平有什么印象？

sentences.en: Well, it wasn't my impression of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那并不是我对此的印象。

sentences.en: It was the way it was, you know.
sentences.zh: 当时的情况就是那样，你知道的。

sentences.en: There wasn't any level of care.
sentences.zh: 根本谈不上什么护理水平。

sentences.en: There was no such thing as emergency medicine
sentences.zh: 那时根本没有急诊医学这回事，

sentences.en: or any of the things we now look back on and think,
sentences.zh: 或者说，我们现在回过头来看，会觉得，

sentences.en: well, what the hell was going on?
sentences.zh: 天哪，当时到底在搞什么？
我的意思是，根本没人受过培训。

sentences.en: He could see that what was going on was effectively a public health crisis
sentences.zh: 他看出当时的情况实际上是一场公共卫生危机，

sentences.en: that was disproportionately affecting black neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 而且对黑人社区的影响尤为严重。

sentences.en: But then one day, Hallen came across an article in the local paper
sentences.zh: 但后来有一天，哈伦在当地报纸上看到了一篇文章，

sentences.en: about a black-operated jobs training program based in the Hill District called Freedom House.
sentences.zh: 讲的是希尔区有一个由黑人运营的职业培训项目，叫“自由之家”。

sentences.en: The article described how Freedom House had rolled out a kind of mobile grocery store
sentences.zh: 文章描述了“自由之家”如何推出了一种流动杂货店，

sentences.en: for black neighborhoods, using trucks to bring fresh vegetables to people's doors.
sentences.zh: 专门服务黑人社区，用卡车把新鲜蔬菜送到人们家门口。

sentences.en: And, well, health care is terrible in the Hill District.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，希尔区的医疗保健状况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: If they could run a grocery van around,
sentences.zh: 如果他们能开着杂货车到处跑，

sentences.en: why can't we run a medical van around or something like that?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能开着医疗车到处跑呢？

sentences.en: Hallen wasn't envisioning anything like modern emergency medical services.
sentences.zh: 哈伦当时并没有设想过现代急救医疗服务那样的东西。

sentences.en: At first, he just thought Freedom House's trucks could help transport people
sentences.zh: 起初，他只是认为“自由之家”的卡车可以帮忙把人运送

sentences.en: in underserved neighborhoods to the hospital
sentences.zh: 到医疗资源匮乏社区的医院去，

sentences.en: and that they could hire people from the Hill District to drive them.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可以雇佣希尔区的人来开车。

sentences.en: But that's when I got the director of the university hospital on this group as well.
sentences.zh: 但就在那时，我也把大学医院的院长拉进了这个小组。

sentences.en: And, you know, before the first meeting was over,
sentences.zh: 你知道，第一次会议还没结束，

sentences.en: he said, oh my God, we have to go immediately to SAFIR.
sentences.zh: 他就说，天哪，我们必须立刻去找萨法尔。

sentences.en: The experimental study you are about to see is one of 18 similar studies
sentences.zh: 你即将看到的这项实验性研究是 18 项类似研究之一，

sentences.en: during which we compared various methods of artificial respiration.
sentences.zh: 在这些研究中，我们比较了各种人工呼吸方法。

sentences.en: Dr. Peter SAFIR was the head of anesthesiology at the University of Pittsburgh.
sentences.zh: 彼得·萨法尔博士是匹兹堡大学麻醉学系的主任。

sentences.en: And by that time, he was already famous in medical circles.
sentences.zh: 那时，他在医学界已经很有名了。

sentences.en: SAFIR was a pure scientist and a very precise and impatient Austrian.
sentences.zh: 萨法尔是一位纯粹的科学家，也是一位非常严谨且缺乏耐心的奥地利人。

sentences.en: We simulated field conditions by selecting as subjects men and women of various body types.
sentences.zh: 我们通过选择各种体型的人作为受试者来模拟现场条件。

sentences.en: This is a film of SAFIR from 1951,
sentences.zh: 这是一部 1951 年拍摄的关于萨法尔的影片，

sentences.en: demonstrating a new technique he developed for resuscitation,
sentences.zh: 展示了他开发的一种新的复苏技术，
也就是我们今天所说的 CPR（心肺复苏术）。

sentences.en: To help orient you, we have made a diagram of the experimental setup.
sentences.zh: 为了方便理解，我们制作了一张实验装置图。

sentences.en: SAFIR understood that, to be effective,
sentences.zh: 萨法尔明白，要达到效果，

sentences.en: resuscitation needed to be started immediately by the first person on the scene.
sentences.zh: 复苏必须由现场的第一目击者立即开始。

sentences.en: But he faced heavy resistance from the medical community,
sentences.zh: 但他遭到了医学界的强烈抵制，

sentences.en: which felt the general public couldn't be trusted with such specialized knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们认为不能信任普通大众去掌握这种专业知识。
于是萨法尔进行了一项实验。

sentences.en: By anesthetizing and curarizing these subjects,
sentences.zh: 通过对这些受试者进行麻醉和箭毒处理，
我们模拟了窒息瘫痪的受害者。

sentences.en: SAFIR paralyzed a group of volunteers using a chemical compound from the Amazon,
sentences.zh: 萨法尔用一种来自亚马逊的化合物麻痹了一组志愿者，
这种化合物通常用于涂抹在毒箭上。

sentences.en: Let's just say medical testing has changed a lot.
sentences.zh: 只能说医学测试已经发生了翻天覆地的变化。

sentences.en: Once the volunteers could no longer breathe on their own,
sentences.zh: 一旦志愿者无法再自主呼吸，

sentences.en: SAFIR had untrained laypeople use CPR to keep those volunteers alive.
sentences.zh: 萨法尔就让未经培训的普通人使用 CPR 来维持这些志愿者的生命。

sentences.en: And when I say untrained laypeople,
sentences.zh: 当我提到未经培训的普通人时，

sentences.en: This boy scout will perform mouth-to-airway breathing.
sentences.zh: 这位童子军将演示口对气道呼吸法。

sentences.en: Ultimately, SAFIR's views would be vindicated.
sentences.zh: 最终，萨法尔的观点得到了证实。

sentences.en: And for his effort, he'd forever be known as the father of CPR.
sentences.zh: 而凭借他的努力，他将永远被称为“CPR 之父”。

sentences.en: Hallin already knew some of this when he walked into Peter SAFIR's office in 1966.
sentences.zh: 1966 年，当哈伦走进彼得·萨法尔的办公室时，他已经了解了一些情况。

sentences.en: But nothing could have prepared him for what actually happened.
sentences.zh: 但没有什么能让他为接下来发生的事情做好准备。

sentences.en: Within seconds of greeting Hallin and the Freedom House team,
sentences.zh: 在问候哈伦和“自由之家”团队后的几秒钟内，

sentences.en: the wiry and energetic SAFIR began to unleash a torrent of ideas.
sentences.zh: 精干而充满活力的萨法尔就开始滔滔不绝地提出各种想法。

sentences.en: Basically, he said, you are just what I'm looking for.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他说，你们正是我要找的人。

sentences.en: I've been trying to figure out how to take rescue breathing and the rest out on the street
sentences.zh: 我一直想弄清楚如何把人工呼吸和其他急救措施带到街头，

sentences.en: and to train people how to do that.

sentences.zh: 但萨法尔并没有就此止步。

sentences.en: He wasn't content to just teach some van drivers CPR.
sentences.zh: 他不满足于仅仅教几个货车司机做 CPR。

sentences.en: I said, let's go beyond that.
sentences.zh: 我说，让我们超越这一点。

sentences.en: Let's train them to be professionals as well.
sentences.zh: 让我们把他们也培养成专业人员。

sentences.en: Professionals who could provide high-quality medical care
sentences.zh: 这些专业人员可以在病人被送往医院之前，

sentences.en: before the person was even taken to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 就提供高质量的医疗护理。

sentences.en: It was not go to the scene, pick up a patient,
sentences.zh: 那不是去现场、接上病人、

sentences.en: transport to a hospital, and then start care.
sentences.zh: 运送到医院，然后再开始护理。

sentences.en: It was emergency treatment right there on the pavement.
sentences.zh: 而是直接在马路上进行紧急治疗。
萨法尔主张，救护车不应只是改装的货运空间，

sentences.en: SAFIR argued that ambulances should be mobile intensive care units
sentences.zh: 而应该是移动的重症监护室，

sentences.en: staffed by professionals trained to use cardiac monitors,
sentences.zh: 配备受过专业训练的人员，能够使用心脏监护仪、

sentences.en: administer medication, and anything else that might keep a patient alive.
sentences.zh: 施用药物，以及采取任何可能维持病人生命的措施。

sentences.en: Hallin and the others could barely keep up.
sentences.zh: 哈伦和其他人都快跟不上他的节奏了。

sentences.en: SAFIR wasn't proposing a simple update to the existing system,
sentences.zh: 萨法尔提出的不仅仅是对现有系统的简单升级，

sentences.en: but it changed the whole culture of pre-hospital care.
sentences.zh: 而是改变了整个院前急救的文化。

sentences.en: And he wanted to do it using Freedom House.
sentences.zh: 而且他想通过“自由之家”来实现这一目标。

sentences.en: I think somebody said, well, how big?
sentences.zh: 我想有人问，规模有多大？

sentences.en: What are we talking about here?
He said, I can teach, I can remember this,
And, you know, inside of a half an hour,
we realized that there was just something going on here
sentences.zh: 我们就意识到这里正在发生的事情，

sentences.en: which was way beyond anything that we had thought of.
sentences.zh: 远远超出了我们之前的任何设想。

sentences.en: SAFIR set about designing advanced ambulances
sentences.zh: 萨法尔着手设计先进的救护车，

sentences.en: and an intense 300-hour course whose graduates would be
sentences.zh: 并开设了一门 300 小时的强化课程，毕业生将成为

sentences.en: the world's first comprehensively trained first responders.
sentences.zh: 世界上第一批受过全面培训的急救人员。

sentences.en: This wasn't just the birth of a profession,
sentences.zh: 这不仅是一个职业的诞生，

sentences.en: but of a whole new branch of medicine.
sentences.zh: 更是一个全新的医学分支的诞生。

sentences.en: It would become a vital link in the chain,
sentences.zh: 它将成为生命链中至关重要的一环，

sentences.en: with a subculture all its own.
sentences.zh: 并拥有自己独特的亚文化。

sentences.en: And the world's first fully trained paramedics
sentences.zh: 而世界上第一批训练有素的护理人员，

sentences.en: would be staffed exclusively with young black men
sentences.zh: 将全部由来自匹兹堡希尔区的年轻黑人男性组成。

sentences.en: from the Hill District of Pittsburgh.
And the people that worked there
sentences.zh: 都被贴上了“无法就业”的标签。
“自由之家”招募的许多第一批学员，

sentences.en: Freedom House recruited many of its first students
sentences.zh: 都是直接从街上找来的，
他们大多数人只是很高兴能找到一份好工作，

sentences.en: most of whom were just happy to land a good job,
sentences.zh: 即使他们对具体细节还不太清楚。

sentences.en: even if they were a little fuzzy on the details.
sentences.zh: 约翰·穆恩并不在第一批学员中。

sentences.en: John Moon wasn't part of that first class.
He signed up a little later.

sentences.zh: 尽管他认为这个机会不可思议，

sentences.en: as incredible as he thought the opportunity was,
sentences.zh: 但他并没有完全理解自己即将投身于什么样的工作。

sentences.en: he didn't fully understand what he was getting into.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，他只是很兴奋，

sentences.en: On some level, he was just excited
sentences.zh: 终于能穿上那件制服了，

sentences.en: to finally be wearing the uniform
sentences.zh: 就是他在第一晚看到的那个很酷的徽章。

sentences.en: with the cool emblem that he saw on the first night.

sentences.zh: 如果有人给你买了一套 1000 美元的西装，

sentences.en: If someone bought you a $1,000 suit
and just gave it to you
sentences.zh: 然后说，穿着它在街上走走就行了，

sentences.en: and said, just walk up and down the street in it,
I was at the point where,

sentences.zh: 这就是帮助别人所需要的全部东西。

sentences.en: That's all it takes to help people.

sentences.zh: 这需要付出的远不止这些。

sentences.en: It took a little bit more than that.

sentences.zh: 穆恩和其他人接受了一系列

sentences.en: Moon and the others underwent a battery

sentences.zh: 和医疗专业人员的面试。
他们学习了解剖学、生理学、CPR、
高级急救、护理和防御性驾驶。

sentences.en: advanced first aid, nursing, and defensive driving.
sentences.zh: 起初是在萨法尔的指导下，
但后来是在“自由之家”的第一位医疗主任的指导下。

sentences.en: but later under Freedom House's first medical director.
sentences.zh: 那是一位 30 岁的白人女医生，
之前没有任何救护车工作经验，
我们起初对她持怀疑态度，

sentences.en: And we looked at her with skepticism

sentences.zh: 她的心是和我们在一起的，

sentences.en: that her heart was with us,
sentences.zh: 她就真的没有什么做错的地方了。

sentences.en: there was really nothing she could do wrong.

sentences.zh: 卡罗琳让学员们能够进入
医院的几乎每一个部门。

sentences.en: to almost every department of the hospital.
She had them work in the morgue,

sentences.zh: 如果他们要把重症监护室带到街头，

sentences.en: if they were going to bring the ICU to the street,
sentences.zh: 他们就必须掌握重症监护室里发生的一切。

sentences.en: they had to master everything that happened in an ICU.
and the advantages of classroom training
sentences.zh: 而课堂培训的优势在于

sentences.en: for us at that particular time is
sentences.zh: 对我们当时的情况来说

sentences.en: we would learn a procedure in class,
sentences.zh: 我们会在课堂上学习一套流程

sentences.en: or she would teach it to us,
and then we would go out
after we got out of class
and perform that procedure on a person.
sentences.zh: 去对真人实施那套流程。
而“自由之家”的医护人员

sentences.en: to perform that procedure outside of a hospital.
sentences.zh: 在医院外实施这些流程的人。

sentences.en: to use Narcan to reverse an overdose
sentences.zh: 使用纳洛酮逆转药物过量的人

sentences.en: and the first to save a patient
by shocking their heart in the field.
sentences.zh: 在现场电击心脏来挽救病人的人。

sentences.en: Moon told me that the biggest first
sentences.zh: 穆恩告诉我，他个人经历过

sentences.en: came on a call where Nancy Caroline
sentences.zh: 发生在一通有南希·卡罗琳

sentences.en: It was a patient having trouble breathing.
sentences.zh: 那是一位呼吸困难的病人。
他当时已经失去意识了。

sentences.en: So Moon started calling it in.
sentences.zh: 于是穆恩开始汇报情况。

sentences.en: But then Nancy Caroline stopped him.
sentences.zh: 但南希·卡罗琳制止了他。

sentences.en: Moon thinks he was the first paramedic
sentences.zh: 穆恩认为他是第一位被要求

sentences.en: to intubate someone in the field.
I wasn't able to confirm that.

sentences.zh: 是一项极其困难的操作。
即使是在医院环境下也是如此。

sentences.en: Moon says he was scared to death.
